questions.explanation: Areas must allow equipment siting, separation of raw/RTE food and satisfactory workflows.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Raw food preparation areas and high-risk preparation areas should be provided with:

options.label: B
options.text: Only one washbasin for the whole premises

options.label: D
options.text: Separate equipment and separate washing facilities

questions.explanation: They need separate equipment and separate facilities for handwashing and washing utensils.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Work areas in a food premises should be:
questions.explanation: Colour-coding helps eliminate cross-contamination between raw and high-risk work.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: A separate area should be provided for:
questions.explanation: The text recommends a separate de-boxing area to avoid contamination from external packaging.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The workflow in food premises should be linear and progress in a uniform direction from:
questions.explanation: Linear workflow runs from raw material to finished product.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Hot water in food premises should be around:
questions.explanation: Hot water should be around 60°C; warm water from spray taps around 35–40°C.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Warm water from spray taps should be around:
questions.explanation: Spray taps provide warm water at around 35°C to 40°C.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Washbasins should be positioned:

options.label: D
options.text: Close to workstations and at the entrance of large food rooms

questions.explanation: Handwash basins are placed close to workstations and at the entrance of large food rooms.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Flexible gas pipes should be used to:

options.label: A
options.text: Allow movement of equipment for cleaning

questions.explanation: Flexible connectors let equipment be moved out for thorough cleaning.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Electrical supplies should be fitted with:
questions.explanation: Accessible cut-out (isolator) switches are required; trailing wires must be avoided.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which type of electrical socket is preferred in food premises?
questions.explanation: Waterproof sockets are preferred and trailing wires must be avoided.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Toilets for staff must be separated from food rooms by:
questions.explanation: Staff toilets should be separated from food rooms by ventilated spaces.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Drainage must be adequate to remove:
questions.explanation: Drainage must remove peak loads quickly without flooding.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Steam- and heat-producing appliances require:
questions.explanation: Suitable hoods are needed over steam- and heat-producing appliances, e.g. a cooker hood.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: High standards of lighting are necessary to:

options.label: D
options.text: Enable cleaning and provide safe, satisfactory working conditions

questions.explanation: Good lighting allows cleaning and safe working; air conditioning controls temperature, condensation and humidity.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Air conditioning in food premises helps to reduce:
questions.explanation: Air conditioning ensures reasonable working conditions and reduces condensation and humidity.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Ceilings in food premises should be:

options.label: C
options.text: Smooth, fire-resistant, non-flaking, light-coloured and coved at wall joints

questions.explanation: Ceilings must be smooth, clean, fire-resistant, non-flaking, light-coloured, coved and easy to clean.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Floors should slope sufficiently so that:
questions.explanation: Where necessary floors should slope to trapped gullies for drainage.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Floor surfaces in food areas should be all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Floors must be clean, hard-wearing, waterproof, anti-slip and free from crevices.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Wall finishes should be:

options.label: A
options.text: Smooth, waterproof, non-flaking, hard-wearing and light-coloured

questions.explanation: Wall finishes must be clean, smooth, waterproof, non-flaking, hard-wearing and light-coloured.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which type of container is preferred for internal waste?
questions.explanation: Disposable polythene sacks in sack holders, or bins with foot-operated lids, are preferred internally.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Polythene sacks should be tied securely when full and placed:
questions.explanation: Full sacks are tied securely and placed in the external waste receptacle.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: After emptying, reusable waste containers should be:

options.label: D
options.text: Roughly cleaned before being brought back into the food room

questions.explanation: They must be roughly cleaned before returning to the food room.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Containers used for storage of refuse:

options.label: A
options.text: Must not be reused for the storage of food

options.label: B
options.text: May be used for open food

options.label: C
options.text: May be reused for food storage

options.label: D
options.text: Should be kept in the kitchen

questions.explanation: Refuse containers must never be reused for storing food.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Dustbins used outside must have:

options.label: C
options.text: Tight-fitting lids and should not overflow

questions.explanation: They need tight-fitting lids, must not overflow and must be waterproof and hard-wearing.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Hands should be washed after:

options.label: C
options.text: Emptying refuse containers and handling waste

questions.explanation: Washing hands after handling refuse/waste prevents contamination.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: All food handling equipment should be designed and constructed to:

options.label: C
options.text: Be fixed permanently to the floor

options.label: D
options.text: Minimise harbourage of soil, bacteria or pests and be easy to clean and disinfect

questions.explanation: Design must minimise harbourage and permit thorough cleaning and disinfection.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food contact surfaces must be all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Surfaces should be smooth, waterproof, non-toxic, non-flaking, non-rusting and hard-wearing.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which material is appropriate for most food equipment?
questions.explanation: Stainless steel is appropriate for most equipment.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: In the recommended colour-coding system, RED equipment is usually used for:
questions.explanation: Red = raw food, yellow = cooked food, green = salad vegetables.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: In the recommended colour-coding system, YELLOW equipment is usually used for:
questions.explanation: Yellow is used for cooked food.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Equipment should be mobile mainly to:

options.label: C
options.text: Facilitate its removal for cleaning, especially when sited close to walls

questions.explanation: Mobility allows removal for cleaning, particularly where equipment sits close to walls.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: All guards on equipment must be:
questions.explanation: Guards must be capable of being thoroughly cleaned.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which equipment must NOT be used in a food premises?

options.label: C
options.text: Cracked, chipped, broken or badly pitted equipment

questions.explanation: Cracked, chipped, broken and badly pitted equipment must not be used.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Adequate refrigeration to cater for peak demand is essential to:
questions.explanation: Refrigeration sized for peak demand prevents bacterial multiplication.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Premises that are unsafe can be:
questions.explanation: The text notes that unsafe premises can be closed.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Premises must be kept:

options.label: B
options.text: Clean and in good repair and condition

questions.explanation: Premises must be kept clean and in good repair and condition, and be capable of thorough cleaning and disinfection.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Rats and cockroaches are often found living in:

options.label: B
options.text: Sewers, rubbish and accumulations of rotting debris

questions.explanation: Cockroaches in particular live in sewers and rubbish; rats also live in sewers and amongst refuse.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food premises attract pests because they provide:
questions.explanation: Food, warmth, harbourage and moisture are the four attractions for pests.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: How may raw materials and packaging bring pests into the premises?

options.label: D
options.text: Pests may be carried in with deliveries

questions.explanation: Raw materials including packaging may bring pests into the premises.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The common food pests in the food industry include:
questions.explanation: The chapter lists rodents (rats and mice) and insects (flies, moths, cockroaches, stored product insects, ants).
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which of these is a rodent found in the food industry?
questions.explanation: Brown rat and black rat are the rodents listed.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as an insect pest?
questions.explanation: Moth larvae, house flies, German cockroach and stored product insects are insects.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Reasons for pest control include all of the following EXCEPT:

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent the spread of disease

options.label: B
options.text: To prevent loss of custom and profit

options.label: D
options.text: To increase the number of pests for study

questions.explanation: Control aims to prevent disease spread, contamination, damage, loss of custom, loss of staff and prosecution.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Gnawing by rodents can cause:

options.label: A
options.text: Fires (gnawing electric cables) and flooding (gnawing pipes)

questions.explanation: Pest damage includes fires from gnawed cables and flooding from gnawed pipes.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Staff may be lost from an infested premises because:

options.label: D
options.text: They will not wish to work there

questions.explanation: Keeping control avoids losing staff who will not work in infested premises.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Failure to control pests may result in:
questions.explanation: Control is needed to comply with the law and avoid being fined or closed.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Pests require which three things to survive?
questions.explanation: Denial of security/shelter and food is the first line of defence.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Denial of these environmental factors is described as:

options.label: D
options.text: The first line of defence against possible infestations

questions.explanation: Environmental control (denial of access, food and harbourage) is the first line of defence.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Doorways can be protected from pests with:

options.label: D
options.text: Hanging plastic strips or air curtains

questions.explanation: Hanging plastic strips and air curtains protect doorways.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The bottom of wooden doors should be protected with:
questions.explanation: Metal plates prevent rodents gnawing at the base of wooden doors.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Access holes and other openings should be sealed with:

options.label: D
options.text: Mortar, cement, metal sheets or mesh

questions.explanation: Openings must be sealed with hard materials such as mortar, cement, metal sheets or mesh.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Under environmental control, food on display or awaiting preparation should be:
questions.explanation: Food on display or awaiting preparation must always be kept covered.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: To prevent breeding, food should be stored:

options.label: B
options.text: Off the floor and clear of walls to allow regular inspection

questions.explanation: Food is stored off the floor and clear of walls for inspection and cleaning.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Deliveries of raw materials and packaging must be checked for:
questions.explanation: All deliveries must be checked for pests.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Damaged or contaminated stock in storage should be:
questions.explanation: Damaged or contaminated stock must be removed and destroyed.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which condition helps deny pests harbourage around a building?

options.label: B
options.text: Keeping vegetation and hiding places around the premises removed

questions.explanation: Vegetation and other hiding places around food premises should be removed.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Regular surveys of food premises are carried out to ensure that they are:
questions.explanation: Regular surveys must be carried out to ensure premises are pest-free.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which areas should be examined during a pest survey?

options.label: B
options.text: Food storage rooms, behind equipment, dark undisturbed and waste storage areas

questions.explanation: These are the high-risk areas for pest activity.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign of RODENT infestation?
questions.explanation: Rodent signs include droppings, holes, runs, footprints, chewed paper and gnawing damage.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Live or dead bodies, nests, fur and smell are signs of:
questions.explanation: Nests, fur, smell and bodies are rodent signs.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: 'Rat grease smears' are:
questions.explanation: Greasy black marks along runs result from rats brushing against surfaces.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Scratching sounds, e.g. in the roof space, indicate:
questions.explanation: Scratching noises, footprints/tail marks in dust and bait takes are rodent signs.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of cockroach infestation?
questions.explanation: Cockroach signs include live or dead bodies, larvae/pupae, eggs and egg cases, and a characteristic smell.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Webbing and holes in food are typical signs of:
questions.explanation: Moth webbing and holes in food, plus piles of 'dust' (frass), indicate insect infestation.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Physical control methods are usually preferred because:

options.label: D
options.text: The pest is caught dead or alive and is not able to die in food, equipment or in a difficult to reach place

questions.explanation: Physical control avoids the pest dying in food or inaccessible places.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Examples of physical pest control include:

options.label: A
options.text: Electric fly killers and rodent traps

questions.explanation: Electric fly killers and rodent traps are physical controls.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Rodenticides are used to kill:
questions.explanation: Rodenticides kill rats and mice; insecticides kill insects.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Before using an insecticide, especially fly sprays, you must:

options.label: D
options.text: Close all windows and stay inside

questions.explanation: Food and small utensils must always be removed, and premises and fixed equipment thoroughly cleaned after use.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Infestations of food premises should be dealt with:

options.label: C
options.text: Immediately, with help from an approved pest control operator

questions.explanation: Managers should seek assistance from an approved pest control operator immediately.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Although very important, environmental control alone may:

options.label: C
options.text: Not be entirely successful, so eradication may need physical or chemical control

questions.explanation: Eradication may need to be achieved by physical or chemical control in addition.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Poorly maintained premises will:
questions.explanation: Poor maintenance (holes, broken windows, damaged doors) increases infestations.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Effective cleaning will remove:
questions.explanation: Effective cleaning removes microbiological hazards.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Chemical and physical hazards from defective cleaning equipment or incorrect use/storage of chemicals must be:
questions.explanation: These hazards must be prevented through correct use and storage of chemicals and well-maintained equipment.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Soiling of surfaces and equipment in food businesses is:
questions.explanation: Soiling is unavoidable, so waste must not be allowed to build up to levels which expose food to risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The removal of food residues, dirt and grease is the process of:
questions.explanation: Cleaning removes food residues, dirt and grease.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The chemical used for cleaning is known as a:
questions.explanation: A detergent is the chemical used for cleaning.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Disinfection is the process of:

options.label: D
options.text: Reducing micro-organisms to a safe level

questions.explanation: Disinfection reduces micro-organisms to a safe level.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The chemical used for disinfection is a:
questions.explanation: A disinfectant is used for disinfection.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: A sanitiser is:
questions.explanation: A sanitiser combines the action of a detergent and a disinfectant.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which of these is a reason for cleaning?

options.label: B
options.text: To increase the cost of production

options.label: D
options.text: To remove matter on which bacteria would grow, reducing risk of contamination, food poisoning and spoilage

questions.explanation: Cleaning removes the food/bacteria substrate and reduces contamination, poisoning and spoilage.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Cleaning allows which process to take place on specific equipment and surfaces?
questions.explanation: Cleaning is a prerequisite so that disinfection can be effective.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Cleaning reduces the risk of physical contamination by:

options.label: C
options.text: Removing materials such as glass, paper and metal debris

questions.explanation: Removing debris reduces the risk of physical contamination.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a stated reason for cleaning?

options.label: C
options.text: To promote a good image to customers

options.label: D
options.text: To provide a pleasant and safe working environment

questions.explanation: Cleaning removes materials that would encourage pest infestations, never encourages them.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Cleaning involves the application of energy to a surface. Energy is applied as:
questions.explanation: Energy is applied physically (scrubbing), as heat (hot water) and chemically (detergent).
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Scrubbing is an example of which type of cleaning energy?
questions.explanation: Scrubbing is physical energy.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: A clean surface is one which is free of:
questions.explanation: A clean surface is free from dirt, grease and food residues.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: How can a clean surface be tested?
questions.explanation: A clean surface can be tested with a white paper tissue.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: After cleaning, hot water at what temperature may be used to destroy bacteria that remain?
questions.explanation: Hot water at 82°C, or a chemical disinfectant, is used to destroy remaining bacteria.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Chemical disinfectants need time to work, therefore an appropriate what is essential?
questions.explanation: An appropriate contact time is essential for disinfectants to act.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: To be effective, cleaning must be:

options.label: D
options.text: Planned, organised and implemented in all areas of food premises

questions.explanation: Effective cleaning is planned, organised and implemented throughout.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which of these should a written cleaning schedule state?

options.label: B
options.text: What is to be cleaned and the amount and type of chemical and equipment to use

options.label: C
options.text: Only the name of the manager

questions.explanation: Schedules cover what, how much/which chemicals, who, when/frequency, method, time allowed, safety and checking.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: A cleaning schedule should state who is responsible for:

options.label: D
options.text: Checking that it has been effectively cleaned

questions.explanation: A named person checks that cleaning has been effective.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Separate, colour-coded cloths and equipment are recommended for:
questions.explanation: Colour-coded cloths/equipment prevent cross-contamination between raw and high-risk areas.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Mixing of cleaning chemicals may produce:
questions.explanation: Chemicals should never be mixed; mixing may produce dangerous gases and/or explosion.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: During cleaning, open food must:

options.label: C
options.text: Be covered or not exposed to risk of contamination

questions.explanation: Open food must not be exposed to risk of contamination during cleaning.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: To be effective, chemicals must be:
questions.explanation: Correct dilution is essential, and rinsing with clean water may be required.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Cleaning equipment used for toilets must NOT be:
questions.explanation: Toilet cleaning equipment must never be used in food rooms.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: 'Clear-and-clean-as-you-go' means:

options.label: C
options.text: Clean only at the end of the shift

options.label: D
options.text: Keep work areas clean and tidy, removing spillages and waste packaging immediately

questions.explanation: Clear-and-clean-as-you-go prevents build-up of waste food and dirty equipment.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Walls, floors, drains and equipment legs require regular thorough cleaning and degreasing but are unlikely to require disinfection unless:

options.label: A
options.text: There is a risk of food contamination

options.label: C
options.text: They are in the dry store

questions.explanation: They do not contact food, so disinfection is only needed if there is a contamination risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Ovens and similar devices which use high temperatures to destroy bacteria:

options.label: B
options.text: Do not require disinfection, but the door handles may

options.label: D
options.text: Must be rinsed with disinfectant after each use

questions.explanation: The oven interior is self-disinfecting by heat; door handles may need disinfection.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Floors in preparation areas may be cleaned:
questions.explanation: Preparation area floors are cleaned daily; dry storage floors weekly provided spillages are removed immediately.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Floors in dry storage areas may be cleaned:
questions.explanation: Dry store floors are cleaned weekly if spillages are removed immediately.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which is the correct first stage of the cleaning and disinfection procedure?
questions.explanation: Pre-clean removes loose soil by sweeping, wiping or pre-rinsing.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: During pre-cleaning, loose soil is removed by:

options.label: A
options.text: Sweeping, wiping or pre-rinsing (a disposable paper towel may be used)

questions.explanation: Pre-clean removes loose soil before the main clean.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: In the main clean stage, surface grease and dirt are loosened using:
questions.explanation: Main clean uses hot water and detergent with a brush or cloth.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: During the main clean, soiled or cooled water must be:
questions.explanation: Soiled or cooled wash water must be changed as often as necessary.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The rinse stage involves:

options.label: B
options.text: Removal of loose dirt and detergent using clean hot water

questions.explanation: Rinse removes loose dirt and detergent with clean hot water.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The disinfection stage destroys micro-organisms using heat or a chemical disinfectant and requires:
questions.explanation: Disinfection needs adequate contact time.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The final rinse stage removes:
questions.explanation: Final rinse removes disinfectant; it is often unnecessary.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The preferred method of drying is:
questions.explanation: Natural air-drying is preferred; otherwise single-use paper towels or a clean dry cloth.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: When cleaning a work surface, you should first:
questions.explanation: Pre-clean (remove scraps and waste) comes first.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: When wiping a work surface, you should never place a bucket:
questions.explanation: A bucket must never be placed on the food contact surface.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Suitable gloves should be worn when using:
questions.explanation: Gloves protect hands when using hot water and chemicals.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: In a dishwasher, the wash cycle operates at around:
questions.explanation: The wash cycle is around 60°C and the rinse cycle between 82°C and 88°C.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The rinse cycle of a dishwasher operates between:
questions.explanation: Rinse cycle: 82°C to 88°C.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The sprayer arm jets of a dishwasher must be:
questions.explanation: Blocked jets prevent effective cleaning; the machine must also be correctly stacked.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: After dishwashing, clean utensils should be:
questions.explanation: Clean utensils should be allowed to air-dry.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Soiled utensils should be washed:

options.label: B
options.text: At the end of the week

questions.explanation: Wash soiled items as soon as possible.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Before cleaning electrical equipment, it must be:

options.label: C
options.text: Switched off at the mains and isolated

questions.explanation: Electrical equipment (e.g. slicing machines) must be switched off, isolated and unplugged before cleaning.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: HACCP is a:
questions.explanation: HACCP is a food safety management system which identifies and controls hazards at critical control points.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: HACCP aims to minimise the risk of:

options.label: C
options.text: Food poisoning or food complaints and ensure safer food

questions.explanation: The system minimises the risk of food poisoning/food complaints and ensures safer food.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food safety management systems should be documented and records maintained:

options.label: A
options.text: Proportional to the size of the business

questions.explanation: Records are maintained proportionally to the size of the business.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Records are important to demonstrate that the system is:

options.label: D
options.text: Being implemented satisfactorily and managed effectively

questions.explanation: Records prove satisfactory implementation and effective management.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which of these could be included in HACCP records?

options.label: C
options.text: Temperature monitoring, staff training, pest control and cleaning schedules

questions.explanation: Records can include HACCP documentation, specifications, deliveries, staff training, temperature monitoring, pest control, sampling, complaints and cleaning schedules.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The HACCP system should be reviewed:

options.label: B
options.text: Annually, if there are any changes, or if something goes wrong

questions.explanation: Review annually, on change, or when something goes wrong.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The first HACCP principle is to:

options.label: D
options.text: Identify the hazards and the control measures

questions.explanation: Principle 1: identify hazards (what could go wrong) and the control measures.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: In HACCP, a hazard is:
questions.explanation: A hazard is anything that could go wrong affecting food safety.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The second HACCP principle is to identify:
questions.explanation: Principle 2: identify the CCPs.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: A critical control point (CCP) is a step in preparation or production which:

options.label: C
options.text: Must be controlled as it is critical to food safety

questions.explanation: CCPs must be controlled because they are critical to food safety.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The third HACCP principle is to establish:

options.label: D
options.text: Critical limits for control measures at each CCP

questions.explanation: Principle 3: establish critical limits at each CCP.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The example of a critical limit given in the chapter is cooking food to a core temperature of:
questions.explanation: Cooking food to a core temperature of 75°C is a typical critical limit.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The fourth HACCP principle is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Monitor (check) the control measures at each CCP to ensure the process is under control

questions.explanation: Principle 4: monitor control measures at each CCP.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The fifth HACCP principle is to establish:

options.label: A
options.text: Corrective actions to be taken if critical limits are breached

questions.explanation: Principle 5: corrective action when something goes wrong.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The sixth HACCP principle is to establish procedures for:

options.label: A
options.text: Verification, i.e. prove that the HACCP system is working

questions.explanation: Principle 6: verification.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The seventh HACCP principle is to establish:

options.label: D
options.text: Documentation and records for the HACCP system

questions.explanation: Principle 7: documentation and records.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: It is essential to purchase food from:

options.label: C
options.text: Approved suppliers with a commitment to high standards of food hygiene

questions.explanation: Approved suppliers demonstrate a commitment to high hygiene standards.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: To minimise hazards from supplies, you should select:

options.label: B
options.text: The least hazardous materials/ingredients, e.g. pasteurised egg and ready-prepared vegetables

questions.explanation: Choosing least hazardous materials (pasteurised egg, prepared vegetables) reduces risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: When specifying a product, you should include:

options.label: A
options.text: The standard and quality required and the delivery temperature

questions.explanation: Specifications should state standard, quality and delivery temperature; branded products are usually preferable.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The main hazards associated with deliveries are:

options.label: C
options.text: Contaminated food and multiplication of bacteria from delays before refrigeration

questions.explanation: Contamination and bacterial multiplication from prolonged delays are the main hazards.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: High-risk food should be delivered:
questions.explanation: High-risk food: below 5°C; frozen food: at -18°C.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Frozen food should be delivered at:
questions.explanation: Frozen delivery temperature is -18°C.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: All deliveries should be checked for:

options.label: A
options.text: Freshness, temperature, colour, odour, contamination, infestation and satisfactory packaging and labelling

questions.explanation: All food must be inspected before placing in storage.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which delivery should be REJECTED?
questions.explanation: Reject perishable food above 5°C and frozen food which is not solid.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: A delivery from an unapproved source should be:
questions.explanation: Food from unapproved sources must be rejected.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food with evidence of pest activity should be:
questions.explanation: Any food with evidence of pest activity must be rejected.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food which is not covered or has damaged packaging should be:
questions.explanation: Uncovered food and damaged packaging present contamination risk and are rejected.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: If a delivery is rejected, who should usually be notified?
questions.explanation: The supervisor and the supplier should usually be notified.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: As far as practicable, external packaging should NOT be brought:

options.label: A
options.text: Into food preparation areas; a separate de-boxing area is recommended

questions.explanation: Use a separate de-boxing area to keep external packaging out of preparation areas.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Unloading should be completed:
questions.explanation: Quick unloading, with trained staff, prevents contamination and temperature abuse.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Delivery records should be retained to enable:

options.label: A
options.text: Traceability in the event of a food complaint

questions.explanation: Records provide traceability if there is a food complaint.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Failure to ensure satisfactory storage conditions will result in:

options.label: A
options.text: Hazards, mould, spoilt food, discolouration, staleness and pest infestation

questions.explanation: Poor storage causes contamination, bacterial multiplication, mould, spoilage, discolouration, staleness and pests.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Rooms used for storage of cereals, dried and canned foods should be:

options.label: C
options.text: Suitable for the purpose, vermin-proof, clean and tidy

questions.explanation: Dry stores must be suitable, vermin-proof, clean and tidy.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which is a hazard encountered in dry food stores?
questions.explanation: Hazards include dirty delivery trays, pests, damaged cartons, rusty cans, out-of-date stock, soil from root vegetables and chemicals.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: In dry stores, food should be stored at least:
questions.explanation: Food should be at least 15 cm above the floor for inspection and cleaning.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which shelving is recommended in dry stores?

options.label: B
options.text: Tubular stainless steel racks or mobile rodent-proof bins

options.label: C
options.text: Open wire baskets on the ground

questions.explanation: Tubular stainless steel racks or mobile rodent-proof bins are recommended.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food in dry stores should be stored away from:

options.label: B
options.text: Walls and pipes affected by condensation

questions.explanation: Avoid walls and pipes where condensation forms.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Potatoes should be stored in the dark to prevent:
questions.explanation: Dark storage prevents sprouting and greening (which produces solanine).
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Blown, badly dented, seam-damaged, holed or rusty cans must be:
questions.explanation: Such cans must be disposed of.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Fruit should be examined regularly because:
questions.explanation: Mould spreads rapidly through fruit.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: High-risk and perishable foods should be stored under refrigeration to:

options.label: A
options.text: Prevent most pathogenic bacteria from multiplying and slow the rate of spoilage

questions.explanation: Refrigeration slows pathogen multiplication and spoilage.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Refrigerators and freezers should be sited:

options.label: A
options.text: In well-ventilated areas away from heat sources and direct sunlight

questions.explanation: Away from heat sources such as ovens and the rays of the sun.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Refrigerators usually operate between:
questions.explanation: Chilled storage operates between 1°C and 4°C.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The display temperature of a refrigerator should be recorded:
questions.explanation: Display temperature is checked every time the fridge is used and recorded at least twice a day.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The actual food temperature in a refrigerator should be checked and recorded:

options.label: A
options.text: At least weekly and whenever display temperature is unsatisfactory

questions.explanation: Food temperature is checked at least weekly and whenever the display reading is unsatisfactory.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: A temporary rise in display temperature occurs if:

options.label: B
options.text: Doors are left open or a large quantity of food/drink at room temperature is loaded

questions.explanation: Door opening and loading warm items cause temporary rises; temperatures should return to normal quickly.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: If raw and high-risk food must be in the same refrigerator, raw food must be placed:
questions.explanation: Raw food goes at the bottom to prevent drip contamination.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food should be covered in the refrigerator to prevent:

options.label: A
options.text: Drying out, cross-contamination and absorption of odour

questions.explanation: Covering prevents drying, cross-contamination and odour absorption.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Foods such as lettuce, tomatoes and cucumbers must be protected from:
questions.explanation: Care is needed to protect these foods from dripping blood.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Refrigerators must NOT be:
questions.explanation: Never overload; leave space for air circulation and don't block cooling units.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Only which foods should be stored in the refrigerator?

options.label: D
options.text: Perishable foods, including vacuum packs and pasteurised cans of meat

questions.explanation: Only perishable foods belong in the fridge.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: New stock should be placed behind existing stock to:
questions.explanation: Placing new stock behind facilitates stock rotation.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Opened or part-used cans, especially acidic foods, must NOT be left in the can because this may result in:
questions.explanation: Acid foods react with the can, causing chemical contamination; decant into a suitable container, cover and refrigerate.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Most refrigeration units defrost automatically and should be cleaned and disinfected at least:
questions.explanation: Clean and disinfect at least weekly, following the manufacturer's instructions.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Staff should be told not to keep the refrigerator door open:
questions.explanation: Keeping the door open longer than necessary raises temperature.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: If a fridge temperature remains too high, a possible cause is:

options.label: D
options.text: Overloading or a thermostat set too high

questions.explanation: Overloading/blocking a shelf or a thermostat set too high are common causes; inform your supervisor.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: If the fridge problem cannot be solved:

options.label: A
options.text: An engineer should be brought in

questions.explanation: Call in an engineer; move food to an alternative fridge unless it has been above 5°C for more than 4 hours, when it should be destroyed.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food that has been above 5°C for more than 4 hours should be:
questions.explanation: Destroy the food if it has been above 5°C for more than 4 hours.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Commercial freezers should operate at:
questions.explanation: Commercial freezers operate at -18°C.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: At -18°C, food will keep for a reasonable time with:
questions.explanation: There is no bacterial growth, although spores and pathogens survive.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: If the freezer temperature rises above -10°C, spoilage organisms (especially moulds and yeasts):
questions.explanation: Above -10°C, moulds and yeasts cause spoilage.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Freezer burn is caused by:
questions.explanation: Freezer burn is dehydration of the food, prevented by suitable packaging.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: When checking a delivery of frozen food, the temperature may be checked:

options.label: A
options.text: Only on the outside of the box

options.label: C
options.text: Between the packs of frozen food

questions.explanation: Check between the packs; if -15°C or lower, move to the freezer as quickly as possible.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: If a delivery of frozen food is not frozen solid it should be:
questions.explanation: Reject food that is not frozen solid and advise management.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: New frozen stock should always be placed:
questions.explanation: Place new stock below or behind existing food.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food must not be stored above the freezer:
questions.explanation: Do not exceed the load line, and observe manufacturer's maximum storage time.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: When frozen raw food has started to thaw, you should:

options.label: D
options.text: Complete the thawing process and cook immediately

questions.explanation: Complete thawing and cook immediately; never refreeze thawed food.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which foods should be completely thawed before cooking?
questions.explanation: Most frozen food can be cooked immediately, but poultry and large joints must be fully thawed.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The area used for thawing raw meat must never be used for:

options.label: A
options.text: Cooked food which is cooling prior to refrigeration

questions.explanation: Never use the raw thawing area for cooked food that is cooling.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Thawing of raw food is best carried out at around:
questions.explanation: Around 10°C is best for thawing raw food; sufficient time must be allowed.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Thawing can also be achieved using clean, cold running water below:
questions.explanation: Clean, cold running water below 15°C may be used, avoiding cross-contamination.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Thawing in a microwave oven requires care because of:
questions.explanation: Uneven heating is a risk; follow manufacturer's instructions.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Once frozen food is completely thawed, it must be immediately:
questions.explanation: Store below 5°C or cook immediately to avoid bacterial multiplication.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Areas used for thawing should be:
questions.explanation: Thawing areas must be thoroughly cleaned and disinfected after use.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Stock rotation rule is:
questions.explanation: First in, first out ensures older food is used first.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Satisfactory stock rotation is essential to:

options.label: A
options.text: Avoid spoilage, reduce the risk of pest infestation and ensure good quality food

questions.explanation: Rotation prevents spoilage, reduces pest risk and ensures quality.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Date codes on high-risk food should be checked:
questions.explanation: High-risk date codes are checked daily; weekly checks may suffice for low-risk products.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The date code on food:

options.label: A
options.text: Must never be altered and food must not be sold after this date

options.label: B
options.text: May be extended if food looks fine

questions.explanation: The date code must never be altered, and date-expired food should be disposed of.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The shelf life of food always depends on:
questions.explanation: Shelf life depends on satisfactory storage conditions; special requirements should be on the label.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Raw food and ready-to-eat food should be prepared:

options.label: B
options.text: With the same knife wiped clean

options.label: C
options.text: In different areas with separate clean equipment

questions.explanation: Separate areas and equipment prevent cross-contamination.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Raw vegetables should be washed in:

options.label: A
options.text: A separate sink not used for washing utensils

questions.explanation: A separate sink, positioned away from ready-to-eat food, is required.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which wiping cloths are preferred?
questions.explanation: Disposable paper wiping cloths are preferred in preparation.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Inadequate cooking or reheating is a serious hazard because it enables:
questions.explanation: Inadequate cooking/reheating lets pathogens survive.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food should be eaten immediately after cooking or:

options.label: C
options.text: Cooled rapidly to prevent problems from spores

options.label: D
options.text: Left to stand at room temperature

questions.explanation: Rapid cooling prevents spore-related problems.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Reheated food should never be:
questions.explanation: Unused reheated food must be discarded; never reheat more than once.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: When cooking stews and sauces, pans should be:

options.label: D
options.text: Stirred frequently and covered when not stirring

questions.explanation: Frequent stirring and covering prevent burning and physical contamination.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Only which type of spoon should be used for tasting food?
questions.explanation: A clean, disinfected spoon must be used for tasting.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The core temperature should be checked with a:

options.label: B
options.text: Clean, disinfected probe thermometer (avoid fat and gristle)

questions.explanation: Use a clean, disinfected probe thermometer at the thickest part of the food.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: The probe must not touch bone or the surface of the container because this will:
questions.explanation: Bone and container surfaces give false readings.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which is NOT a reliable indicator that food is cooked properly?
questions.explanation: Colour and texture are subjective and not reliable; juices running clear and no blood are used for chicken.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: If cooked food has not achieved 75°C, you should:

options.label: B
options.text: Continue cooking until this temperature is reached

options.label: C
options.text: Reheat in a microwave for a minute

questions.explanation: Continue cooking; if the oven is faulty, inform the supervisor and call the engineer.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food cooked in a microwave should usually be heated throughout to at least:
questions.explanation: Heat throughout to at least 75°C, checked in several places to guard against cold spots.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: When using a microwave, it is essential to know the oven's:
questions.explanation: Know the wattage and allow adequate time; stirring and standing time may be needed.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Domestic microwave ovens are unsuitable for:
questions.explanation: Domestic microwave ovens are unsuitable for commercial operations.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Covering hot holding containers helps to:
questions.explanation: Covering prevents contamination and slows cooling; food should be stirred regularly.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Hazards associated with cooling include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Cooling hazards are bacterial multiplication, toxin production, spore germination and contamination.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: A blast chiller is the safest way to cool food because cooling may be achieved in:
questions.explanation: A blast chiller can cool food in about 90 minutes.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Without a blast chiller, food should be cooled from 60°C to 20°C within:
questions.explanation: 60°C to 20°C within 2 hours, then 20°C to 5°C within a further 4 hours.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Without a blast chiller, food should be cooled from 20°C to 5°C within a further:
questions.explanation: A further 4 hours is allowed from 20°C to 5°C.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Cooling times can be reduced by minimising the size of joints. A maximum weight of what is recommended?
questions.explanation: A maximum joint weight of 2.25 kg is recommended.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Cooling may be done in a ventilated, cool room for up to:
questions.explanation: Up to 2 hours in a ventilated cool room before refrigeration.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Which methods may be used to speed up cooling?
questions.explanation: Ice baths and fans speed cooling; shallow containers help for stews and sauces.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Rice, pasta, vegetables and potatoes can be cooled using:
questions.explanation: Cold running drinking water is used for these foods.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Hot food should not be placed in a refrigerator if it would cause the temperature of stored food to rise above:
questions.explanation: It must not push existing food above 5°C; it may also cause condensation.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: If food is sliced after cooking, it is essential that knives are:
questions.explanation: Knives must be cleaned and disinfected, and no contamination introduced by handlers.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Self-service of open food and buffets present many hazards, in particular from:

options.label: D
options.text: Customers, which are difficult to control

questions.explanation: Customer behaviour at open food buffets is hard to control.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: What is recommended for buffets and retail displays?

options.label: C
options.text: Refrigerated buffets and retail display units

questions.explanation: Refrigerated units are recommended; otherwise display the minimum amount of food.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Serving utensils must be stored properly, especially:
questions.explanation: Ice-cream scoops in particular need proper storage.
questions.sourceTitle: Food Safety Handbook MCQ Practice Bank (Chapters 6–9)

questions.question: Food placed on tables, such as bread rolls, must be:

options.text: Aromatic flavoring bundles added during cooking and removed before serving (sachet = dried spices in cheesecloth; bouquet = fresh herbs tied together)

questions.question: The CIA's approach to "sustainability" in the professional kitchen includes:

options.label: B
options.text: Sourcing locally and seasonally, reducing waste, nose-to-tail cooking, composting, minimizing energy and water use, and choosing sustainable seafood

questions.question: The CIA's philosophy on "the professional chef" emphasizes that a modern chef must be:

options.label: B
options.text: A leader, manager, artist, and scientist who understands food safety, nutrition, costing, sustainability, team management, and global cuisines

options.label: D
options.text: Only focused on classical French cuisine
